summary: Eleven concrete, comment-endorsed developer tools, knowledge systems, and keyboards surfaced from a complete HN front-page comment crawl.
telegram_footer: 11 items surfaced | 30/30 current front-page stories processed | history + run artifact updated.

items.name: PowerSync
items.source_story_title: There's no reason for software to be slow anymore
items.summary: A database sync engine for responsive offline-first applications.
items.why_included: A production customer explicitly recommended it for building offline-first apps.
items.evidence: A commenter said their company uses PowerSync in production and recommends it.

evidence_sources.author: giovannibonetti
evidence_sources.excerpt: My company is a (production) customer, and we recommend it.

items.name: TLA+ Language Server Protocol
items.source_story_title: Rust Glancer: Rust LSP using 100x less RAM
items.summary: A TLA+ language server built to add editor support, including Neovim.
items.why_included: Its user said the quickly assembled server works shockingly well.
items.evidence: The commenter built it for missing TLA+ Neovim support and praised the result.

evidence_sources.author: tombert
evidence_sources.excerpt: I couldn't find good TLA+ bindings for Neovim, so I got Claude to hack together an LSP server for it [1]. It works shockingly well

items.name: JMH
items.source_story_title: There's no reason for software to be slow anymore
items.summary: OpenJDK's harness for rigorous Java and JVM microbenchmarks.
items.why_included: An experienced user called it the standard way to handle Java benchmark pitfalls.
items.evidence: The commenter uses JMH and highlighted its built-in handling of JIT warmup.

evidence_sources.author: eaftan
evidence_sources.excerpt: JMH as the framework to write microbenchmarks. It takes care of dealing with JIT warmup, etc. It's the standard way to write rigorous Java microbenchmarks.

items.name: async-profiler
items.source_story_title: There's no reason for software to be slow anymore
items.summary: A low-overhead Java profiler designed to avoid safepoint sampling bias.
items.why_included: A hands-on user preferred its unbiased profiling over safepoint-based alternatives.
items.evidence: The commenter uses async-profiler and explained why its sampling is more accurate.

evidence_sources.author: eaftan
evidence_sources.excerpt: async-profiler is not biased in this way.

items.name: Grafana OSS observability stack
items.summary: A self-hosted stack for dashboards, logs, metrics, traces, and telemetry collection.
items.why_included: A practitioner said the OSS stack works well across personal and consulting projects.
items.evidence: The commenter runs Grafana, Loki, Prometheus, Tempo, and Alloy with OpenTelemetry.

evidence_sources.author: losingthefight
evidence_sources.excerpt: for all of my personal and consulting jobs, OSS LGTM/P works good for me.

items.name: Open Watcom
items.source_story_title: Everyone says assembly is untyped—everyone is wrong
items.summary: An open-source C, C++, and Fortran toolchain with inline assembly support.
items.why_included: A retro developer enthusiastically endorsed its C inline assembler from frequent use.
items.evidence: The commenter loves and regularly uses the Watcom C inline assembler for retro projects.

evidence_sources.author: bananaboy
evidence_sources.excerpt: I love the Watcom C inline assembler. I use it frequently in my retro projects!

items.name: Quartz
items.source_story_title: Show HN: OzBrain, a shared brain for knowledge between agents and your team
items.summary: A static-site generator for publishing linked Markdown knowledge bases.
items.why_included: A user credited Quartz in a simple, cross-device knowledge system that works well.
items.evidence: The commenter uses Quartz to rebuild a Markdown knowledge site on their server.

evidence_sources.author: fallinditch
evidence_sources.excerpt: A Quartz website builder creates a static site on my server, each MD file is a web page, and rebuilds when a new file is added [2].

items.name: Johnny.Decimal
items.source_story_title: Show HN: OzBrain, a shared brain for knowledge between agents and your team
items.summary: A numbered structure for organizing files, notes, and other personal information.
items.why_included: Its creator showed a low-tech way to give Claude reliable note locations.
items.evidence: The creator uses Johnny.Decimal with Obsidian so Claude can find notes by number.

evidence_sources.author: jen729w
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use an Obsidian vault and my system. "It's at 23.16", I tell Claude. From that it can instantly find my notes and files.

items.name: ZSA Voyager
items.summary: A portable low-profile split mechanical keyboard with a columnar layout.
items.why_included: Multiple owners praised its comfort, build quality, and effect on wrist pain.
items.evidence: Two users described the Voyager as excellent and delightful, with one reporting resolved wrist pain.

evidence_sources.author: Zambyte
evidence_sources.excerpt: Their boards are pricey, but excellent.

evidence_sources.author: masterj
evidence_sources.excerpt: I use the Voyager, and it's a delight! I switched when I was suffering from a lot of wrist pain, and it's never come back.

items.name: Monkeytype
items.summary: A minimal, customizable typing test for practicing speed and accuracy.
items.why_included: A commenter singled it out as their continuing favorite typing tool.
items.evidence: The commenter directly called Monkeytype their favorite.

evidence_sources.author: squigz
evidence_sources.excerpt: Monkeytype is still my favorite https://monkeytype.com/

items.name: Pinky4
items.summary: An open split keyboard with staggered columns and four thumb keys.
items.why_included: A long-term user praised its reachable, comfortable thumb cluster.
items.evidence: The commenter has used Pinky4 for years and finds every thumb key comfortable.

evidence_sources.author: opan
evidence_sources.excerpt: I've been using a Pinky4 for years and all the thumb keys are easy to reach and comfortable.
